subject: Communication
title: Cicero and the Five Canons of Rhetoric
description: A fast breakdown of Cicero and the Five Canons of Rhetoric for builders.

hook.text: Roman senator Cicero turned Greek theory into a practical system that speakers still use today.

buildup.text: He outlined five canons: invention, arrangement, style, memory, and delivery.

discovery.text: Invention is finding your argument. Arrangement is structuring it. Style is choosing your words.

twist.text: Memory and delivery — the two canons we've mostly abandoned — were considered the most important.

climax.text: Cicero memorized hours-long speeches using the method of loci — placing ideas in mental rooms.

punchline.text: Great speeches aren't just written well. They're built.

quiz.question: How many canons of rhetoric did Cicero outline?

details.summary: Cicero organized the art of rhetoric into five canons: invention (finding arguments), arrangement (structuring them), style (choosing language), memory (retaining the speech), and delivery (presenting it). This framework has guided speakers for over two thousand years.
details.whyItMatters: The five canons provide a complete preparation system for any speech. Every modern presentation course still follows this structure, even if unknowingly.
takeaways: Invention means finding the best arguments for your case
Arrangement is the strategic ordering of those arguments
Delivery includes voice, gesture, and physical presence

faq.question: Why is the memory canon often overlooked today?
faq.answer: Modern speakers use notes, teleprompters, and slides, reducing the need for memorization. Ancient orators had no such tools and delivered hour-long speeches from memory using techniques like the method of loci. The skill remains valuable for impromptu speaking.

faq.question: How do the five canons apply to modern presentations?
faq.answer: Research your content (invention), structure your slides logically (arrangement), choose clear language (style), rehearse thoroughly (memory), and practice vocal variety and body language (delivery). The framework maps perfectly to modern presentation preparation.
